data.title: Gold pares gains as Fed-hike risks linger, eyes first weekly rise in three weeks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold pares gains after jumping over 3% earlier in the session
  • Spot silver up nearly 5%, off $38.18/oz lows hit on Wednesday
  • Gold, silver, platinum eye first weekly gain in three weeks

By Sherin Sans

Gold pared gains on Friday as a firm US dollar, rising Treasury yields and a hawkish Federal Reserve outlook kept investors cautious, but bullion remained on track for its first weekly gain in three as bargain buying lifted prices from a 15-month low hit earlier this week.

Spot gold rose nearly 2% to $3,635.81 per ounce by 9:34 a.m. ET (1434 GMT), having risen more than 3% earlier in the session. The metal was on track for a weekly gain of nearly 3% after posting losses in the previous two weeks.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 2.9% to $3,634.30 per ounce.

"This recent bounce looks more like short-covering/profit taking than a change in trend. The Fed is still hiking, real yields are high and the dollar is near multi-month highs. Until one of those shifts, rallies toward $3,750–3,800 could attract sellers," said Zain Vawda, market analyst at Audacity Capital.

The dollar was still close to its highest level in 22 months, making dollar-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies, while the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield rose and was off its recent lows.

Gold fell to its lowest level since late August 2025, at $3,426.35 per ounce, on Wednesday after strong US inflation data boosted expectations that the Fed will keep raising interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

"A return to $5,000 is possible, but not in the first half of the year. Gold needs the Fed to stop hiking and the dollar to roll over. If that happens by mid-2027, a recovery toward $4,500 is realistic," Vawda added.

Rising interest rates diminish gold's appeal by boosting returns on competing interest-bearing assets.

Meanwhile, physical gold demand in key Asian hubs improved this week, with jewellery and investment buying picking up in India, while strong retail purchases in China kept local premiums firm.

Spot silver climbed 5.4% to $43.73 per ounce, platinum gained 2.5% to $1,323.33 per ounce and palladium rose 2.7% to $896.25 per ounce.

All three metals were poised for weekly gains.

data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Bayhorse Silver Inc, (TSXV: BHS) (OTCQB: BHSIF) (FSE: 7KXN) (the "Company" or "Bayhorse") reports on the results received for six drill holes from its seven underground drill holes totaling 886m (2922 ft) into four IP targets that were identified during its 2025 Bayhorse IP survey (Figure 1). The results from one remaining drill hole is pending. Two holes, CR2-2026-1 and CR2-2026-2 were drilled south at shallow angles into IP target CR-2, that was located 121 - 150 m (400 - 495 ft) south of the underground drill station.

Each drill hole intersected the middle of the calculated down dip center elevation of the anomalies. Drill holes into the CR-1 anomaly intersected relatively competent ground, while drill holes into the CR-2 anomaly met with extremely difficult ground conditions.

Diamond drill hole MW-2-2026-00, was planned to intersect the northern, lower rhyolite body at 500 ft downhole and drilled at a 45 dg dip to 130 m (429 ft) north from the drill station and 70 m (231 ft) west of the ground water test well 2024 MW-2 to test the westward extension of a reported 1.5 m (5 ft) grading 1104 g/t (35.46 opt) silver and 1.5 m (5 ft) 770 g/t (23.12 opt) silver mineralization within a mineralized 9 m (30 ft ) zone estimated between 21 - 30 m (70 - 100 ft) downhole as reported in the Company's news release BHS2025-12. Due to ground conditions, this drill hole was terminated at a downhole depth of 365 ft.

The top of the silver bearing rhyolite has been cut and offset by east-directed thrusting, and the overlying segment dyke that has been historically mined has been displaced to the south a minimum of 60 m (200) with a vertical displacement identified by drilling of a minimum 20 m (66 ft). Subsequently, there is significant faulting and fault gouge between the northern and southerly displaced rhyolite section resulting from the displacement of the upper mineralized section to the south. Due to the significant vertical and horizontal structural offset of the rhyolite body, it was only possible to drill low angle holes (-30 to -45 degrees) to intercept the northern section of the mineralized rhyolite from the underground drill station. This prevented any drilling of the northern underlying segment of mineralization, which is estimated to be 60-70 m (198 - 230 ft) north of, and 20-30 m (66-100 ft) below, the bottom of the south displaced section at the 706 m (2330 ft) above sea level.

data.title: Vertex falls on “disappointing” FDA delay on kidney drug review; Vera rises
data.description:
Vertex Pharmaceuticals traded lower on Friday, and rival Vera Therapeutics gained after the U.S. FDA extended its review of the former’s kidney disease drug povetacicept, a decision Leerink Partners identified as “quite disappointing.”

Announcing the revised Feb. 28 target action date issued in connection with its Biologics License Application for povetacicept in IgA nephropathy, Vertex on Wednesday attributed the delay to an information request from the FDA.

The company's stock lost more than 10% after the announcement, its worst intra-day performance since August 2025.

Vera Therapeutics , whose once-weekly injectable branded as Trutakna received the U.S. accelerated approval for IgA nephropathy in July, added ~15% in reaction, recording its best intraday gain since June 2025.

Noting the review extension as “quite disappointing,” Leerink Partners analyst David Risinger, who has an Outperform rating on Vertex , remained hopeful. “We now assume that pove will be approved within the next three months,” Risinger wrote, according to Bloomberg.“Although we cannot predict the FDA label, we are hoping that if blood monitoring is required, it is infrequent and thus does not materially impact commercial prospects,” the analyst added.

Baird analyst Brian Skorney, who has an Underperform rating on Vertex , argued that the delay allows rivals Vera and Otsuka Holdings to extend their lead in the IgAN market with their directly competitive, approved drugs. “In a worst-case scenario, the FDA request is looking closer at potential need for IgG monitoring for povetacicept,” Skorney added.

Raymond James analyst Christopher Raymond argued that the insufficient details provided on the reason for the delay are "likely to fuel bearish speculation around the drug’s safety profile.” Raymond, who has a Market Perform rating on VRTX, says he “can’t argue that this program does not now carry a meaningfully higher level of risk.”

data.title: Bigger Generali stake among options for UniCredit as partnership expands, sources say
data.description:
UniCredit has been weighing a possible increase of its 9% stake in Generali , four people close to the matter said, as Italy's second-biggest bank and the country's largest insurer discuss new commercial accords.

The Generali investment has so far been the only move by UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel in Italy's fast-consolidating banking market.

The veteran dealmaker has just secured control of Germany's Commerzbank , and says UniCredit will grow its domestic market share without any major acquisitions.

Meanwhile, the Generali stake has positioned UniCredit as a counterweight to its main rival Intesa Sanpaolo - which looks set to become the biggest Generali shareholder through a takeover of Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) .

Two of the four people said UniCredit could raise its Generali holding towards the 13.4% stake which is expected to pass from MPS into Intesa's hands.

The outcome of UniCredit's deliberations remains uncertain.

UniCredit and Generali both declined to comment.

By exercising significant influence over Generali, without control, Intesa can book the insurer's profits in its earnings in proportion to the stake, under international accounting rules.

Independent of its Generali stake coming from the MPS deal, Intesa has also built a further 3% stake in the insurer, which it has said it will dispose of.

Intesa CEO Carlo Messina has said he would be happy for UniCredit and Generali to find ways to generate profits together.

UniCredit first unveiled a 4.1% Generali stake , before building it up to the current 9.05%. Crossing 10% requires supervisory approval.

UniCredit and Generali, which already partner in eastern Europe, have been discussing closer commercial ties.

On November 9, Orcel said it was up to Generali to decide whether to accept UniCredit's help, adding that he hoped an agreement could be reached in the coming months.

He has repeatedly said such partnerships do not require UniCredit to control Generali, or a formal combination.

Orcel last week put the value of closer cooperation between UniCredit and Generali at €1.5-€2.0 billion ($1.6-$2.2 billion), with Generali remaining independent and simply agreeing to "innovative" forms of partnership.

A day later, Generali CEO Philippe Donnet said the insurer agrees with Orcel's view of the value the two companies can generate together.($1 = 0.9136 euros)

data.title: Romania's consolidated budget deficit at 3.92% of GDP at end-October
data.description:
Key points:
  • Romania's 2026 deficit target 6.2% of output, finmin warns of risks
  • Government must approve 2027 budget by year-end
  • Romanian funding needs will fall to 248 billion lei in 2027

Romania's consolidated budget deficit shrank to 3.92% of economic output in the first 10 months of the year, Finance Minister Alexandru Nazare said on Friday, from a shortfall of 5.64% in the same period of 2025.

Nazare warned that spending commitments in the final two months of the year were rising, and added that Romania must continue cutting its budget shortfall next year to avoid losing its investment-grade credit rating and keep its access to European Union funds.

The country is aiming to lower its budget deficit, the EU's largest, from more than 9% of economic output in 2024 to 6.2% this year and below 3.0% by 2031.

"Romania cannot afford to stop the fiscal consolidation," Nazare told reporters. "The window for an orderly correction is open but narrowing."

The minority government of Prime Minister Luca Niculescu, appointed after a nearly six-month political impasse, must balance deficit cuts against social pressure to raise state wages and pensions after a two-year cap.

Meanwhile, Romania's public debt has exceeded 60% and is expected to keep growing.

In nominal terms, the deficit stood at 81.9 billion lei ($16.85 billion) at the end of October. Revenue totaled 596.32 billion lei, or 28.6% of output.

Nazare said Romania had about 19 billion lei worth of funding obligations for the rest of the year, including 15 billion lei in wage increases for judges and prosecutors which were challenged but upheld in court.

Romania's funding needs will fall to 248 billion lei next year from this year's 279 billion lei, Nazare said, a respite for the ailing economy where the high borrowing requirements and elevated bond yields are pushing corporate borrowing rates towards double digits.

data.title: Alligator Bioscience completes sale of mitazalimab to Biossil
data.description:
Lund, Sweden – 27 November 2026 – Alligator Bioscience (Nasdaq Stockholm: ATORX) today announced that the sale of all rights and assets related to the CD40 agonist antibody mitazalimab to Biossil Inc. (“Biossil”), communicated on 31 October 2026, has been completed.

All significant closing conditions have been satisfied, and ownership of mitazalimab and responsibility for its further development, manufacturing and patent costs have passed to Biossil. Alligator has received the upfront payment of USD 0.75 million, and remains eligible for milestone payments and royalties on future sales, as described in the press release of 31 October 2026.

“We are pleased to have completed this transaction, which represents an important milestone for Alligator. We would like to thank everyone involved for their dedication and professionalism throughout the process,” said Johan Giléus, CFO, and incoming CEO, of Alligator Bioscience.

For further information, please contact:

Johan Giléus, CFO

E-mail: johan.gileus@alligatorbioscience.com

Phone: +46 (0) 46 540 82 00

The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact person set out above, at 3:45 p.m. CET on 27 November 2026.

About Alligator Bioscience

Alligator is a biotechnology company with financial interests, through milestone payments and royalties on future sales, in two programmes: HLX22, an anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody being developed by Shanghai Henlius Biotech Inc., and mitazalimab, an anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody, including its derivatives, being developed by Biossil, Inc. Alligator also holds an interest in the antibody ALG.APV-527, co-developed with Aptevo Therapeutics Inc., as well as in the bispecific antibody format RUBY™.

Alligator is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ATORX) and headquartered in Lund, Sweden.
